te.title: Pressure spikes in the conveying line
te.sit: Since the dryer changed its sieve screens the pick-up pressure jumps by 10–20 kPa every few minutes and falls back; twice this week PAH-102 has come in. The air flow and the feed look normal. What is wrong?

te.title: Less resin at the same feeder speed
te.sit: Over the last shift the resin rate has drifted down at the same RV-101 speed, and the day-silo vent filter has started to puff. FIC-101 is steady at its set point.

te.title: Line pressure creeping up, air unchanged
te.sit: Over half an hour PT-102 and the other line pressures have crept up while FT-101 and WI-110 have not changed. Bagging says the resin feels sticky.

te.title: The blower works harder for the same air
te.sit: The blower speed and current are higher than last month for the same FT-101 and the same feed. The line pressures are normal.

te.title: Where does the resin go?
te.sit: The silo-A level rises more slowly than WI-110 says it should, although nothing is drawn from it; the line pressures are a little higher than usual.

te.title: The line keeps blocking
te.sit: The line has blocked twice this week although FT-101 is always at its set point of 0.98 kg/s. XI-106 reads 1.2 or more. The dryer started a new grade on Monday.

te.title: Hot conveying air in the afternoon
te.sit: Every afternoon this week TT-103 has crept towards its high alarm with TV-103 wide open.

te.title: PSV-101 roars, PT-102 steady
te.sit: The field operator hears PSV-101 blowing, yet PT-102 on the DCS has not moved for the last hour.

te.title: Blower hot and the air short
te.sit: FIC-101 is at maximum output, the air is below its set point and TT-101 is higher than usual.

te.title: Streamers in the product
te.sit: Bagging complains about angel hair and fines in the bags. After last month's blockages the day shift raised FIC-101 "to be safe".

te.title: Air will not reach its set point
te.sit: FIC-101 output is rising but FT-101 falls slowly; the speed indicator has not moved since this morning.

te.title: Feed rate falls over the shift
te.sit: The day silo was at 19 % at the start of the shift. Nobody has heard from the dryer.

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Pressure spikes in the conveying line (PVC Dilute-Phase Conveying)
meta.caseTitle: Pressure spikes in the conveying line
meta.sit: Since the dryer changed its sieve screens the pick-up pressure jumps by 10–20 kPa every few minutes and falls back; twice this week PAH-102 has come in. The air flow and the feed look normal. What is wrong?

0.1.unit: The unit conveys 18 t/h of suspension PVC resin from the day silo D-100 to the storage silos D-201A/B through a 98 m dilute-phase line (DN150, then DN200 after the step at PI-104). Rotary valve RV-101 (HIC-110) feeds the resin into air from the lobe blower K-101 on a VFD (FIC-101 on FT-101, 0.98 kg/s); after-cooler E-101 holds the air at 40 °C (TIC-103). PIC-102 on the pick-up pressure PT-102 overrides the feeder speed (low select) when the line loads up. Trips: PSHH-102 70 kPa g, FSLL-101 0.70 kg/s, TSHH-103 65 °C stop the feeder (I-1).

rows.what: The pick-up pressure jumps by 10–20 kPa every few minutes and falls back; PAH-102 twice this week
rows.when: Since the dryer changed its sieve screens

rows.what: PT-102 base 47.5 kPa g, spikes to 65.5 kPa g; 8 spikes in 20 min
Air and feed look normal: FT-101 0.982 kg/s, WI-110 17.7–18.2 t/h

0.4.ctx: Normal at design: 18 t/h to silo A, FT-101 0.98 kg/s, PT-102 47.3 kPa g, PI-104 22.5, PI-105 12.4 kPa g, PI-101 ≈ 62 kPa g, II-101 ≈ 113 A, XI-106 1.24. The dryer changed its sieve screens before the complaints started; nothing else was changed on the conveying unit.

R.1.p: Dilute-phase conveying keeps every particle in suspension: the air must move faster than the saltation velocity everywhere, the worst point being the start of the larger DN200 section (XI-106 = v / v_salt there, design 1.24). The line pressure drop is the sum of air friction, acceleration of the solids, solids friction and lift. The lobe blower is a positive-displacement machine: it pushes the air whatever the pressure, so any extra resistance shows at once as a higher PT-102 and PI-101, a little more slip (FT-101 dips) and more motor current. A lump or a local plug adds resistance at one point for as long as it sits there.

R.2.eq: ΔP_line = ΔP_air + ΔP_acc + ΔP_solids,friction + ΔP_lift     v / v_salt ≥ 1.1     P_blower ≈ ṁ·ΔP/(ρ·η)

sym.m: Pick-up pressure PT-102 minus silo pressure
Superficial air velocity (FT-101, pressure, temperature, bore)
Saltation velocity of the resin at that bore and loading
Solids loading ratio WI-110 / FT-101 (≈ 5 kg/kg at design)

Slow steady creep of every line pressure; lab moisture high
PI-104 − PI-105 off design; hissing at the flap; silo gain lower than WI-110

R.5.chk:
1 Is the feed steady before each spike (WI-110, SI-110)?
2 Is the air on set point between spikes (FT-101, XI-106)?
3 Do PI-101 and II-101 move with PT-102?
4 Are the base pressures on design between spikes (PT-102, PI-104, PI-105)?
5 What does the line sound like; what is on the day-silo grid?
6 What changed upstream (dryer, grade, screens)?

rows.info: Since the dryer changed its sieve screens the pick-up pressure jumps by 10–20 kPa every few minutes and falls back; twice this week PAH-102 has come in. The air flow and the feed look normal.
“The line is just running a bit lean on air — turn the air up.”
“The PT-102 transmitter has been playing up since the shutdown.”

1.3.safn: PI-101 reached 80.7 kPa g against PSV-101 set at 90 kPa g; a larger plug lifts the PSV (resin dust at the relief outlet)
1.3.envn: No release while the line stays closed; a PSV lift would vent dusty air
1.3.eqn: II-101 to 147 A (trip 176 A); a full blockage needs the line opened and purged
1.3.prodn: Spikes reach 65.5 kPa g against PSHH-102 at 70 kPa g: one more lump of that size stops the feeder (I-1); a full blockage costs hours of conveying
1.3.ttl: About 4 kPa from the PSHH-102 trip on the largest spike; spikes every few minutes

1.4.why: Between spikes the line is on design and PIC-102 already trims the feed when a spike comes. Stopping now would leave a line full of resin. Investigate within the shift with a stop line.
1.4.park: Stop line: if PT-102 passes 62 kPa g twice in 10 min, or PI-101 passes 85 kPa g, cut HIC-110 to 50 % (about 15 t/h) and keep the air at set point; if PSHH-102 trips, purge the line with air before restarting the feed.

1.5.sp: A reduced, stable condition that stops the problem growing while you investigate (here: feed cut to about 15 t/h, air kept at set point).
1.5.tc: A consequence (a trip, a blockage, a PSV lift) will arrive before the diagnosis is finished unless you act now.

1.6.p: A positive-displacement blower pushes its air whatever the resistance, so a plug anywhere in the line shows at once as a pressure rise from that point back to the blower. A spike with steady feed and steady air means something in the line, not the feed or the air.

ppl.msg: Spikes to 65.5 kPa g, trip at 70; investigating; stop line PT-102 > 62 kPa g twice in 10 min
Walk the conveying line and listen; look at RV-101 and the day-silo grid; take a resin sample
Which sieve screens were fitted, and when? Any lumps on the screens?
Feed may be cut to 15 t/h for a while; tell us about lumps in the bags

1.7.reply: The conveying line is running, but the pick-up pressure jumps every few minutes and has reached the alarm twice. We are checking the line, the feeder and the resin now and will report the cause and the plan within the hour.

2.1.u: Design: 18 t/h resin, FT-101 0.98 kg/s (≈ 0.95 kg/s conveying after the RV-101 leakage), loading ≈ 5.3 kg/kg; PT-102 47.3, PI-104 22.5, PI-105 12.4 kPa g; PI-101 ≈ 62 kPa g; SI-101 ≈ 2 470 rpm, II-101 ≈ 113 A; XI-106 1.24; PSHH-102 70 kPa g, PSV-101 90 kPa g.

rows.what: Where the extra pressure drop sits

rows.where: Field ▸ the line, RV-101, the day-silo grid

2.5.t: cause found within 1 h; fixed within the shift
2.5.sf: no feeder trip, no PSV lift, no blockage
2.5.goal: Bring PT-102 back to a steady 47 kPa g with no spikes for 15 min at 18 t/h within the shift, without a trip, a PSV lift or a blockage, for less than USD 3 000.

2.6.what: PT-102 spikes from 47.5 to as much as 65.5 kPa g and falls back
2.6.when: Every few minutes, at irregular times; since the dryer changed its screens
2.6.where: The conveying line (pick-up to silo); blower and feeder steady
2.6.why: One larger spike trips the feeder (PSHH-102) or lifts PSV-101
2.6.how: Short spikes on a steady base

rows.dist: The air can break up what settles

rows.u: Does anything arrive with the resin (lumps, skins, foreign bodies)?

rows.u: Is the air enough for this resin?

2.10.why: Spikes continue at the same rate; none has reached the trip yet

2.11.what: The pick-up pressure PT-102 of the PVC conveying line
2.11.where: at the start of the line (pick-up), with PI-101, PI-104 and PI-105 following
2.11.how: jumps from 47.5 to as much as 65.5 kPa g 8 times in 20 min and falls back within about 30 s

2.11.when: since the dryer changed its sieve screens, while FT-101, WI-110 and the base pressures between spikes stay on design.

rows.val: the first DN200 run (after the step, to DV-101): slightly dull underneath, surging noise; a bang at a bend a moment ago
rows.means: Something settles briefly at a bend and is blown through

rows.val: RV-101 turning at 18.0 rpm; day silo 60 %; air blowing back up through the rotor into D-100: normal (slight); lumps and hard skins seen on the day-silo grid.
rows.means: Lumps arrive with the feed; the rotor and its leakage are normal

rows.val: silo sample: clean resin, few fines; moisture 0.2 %; bulk density 490 kg/m³.
rows.means: The resin itself is dry and normal

3.2.n: Base ΔP is on design, so the air and resin between lumps convey normally (XI-106 1.24 ≥ 1.1). A spike of about 18 kPa at PT-102 with only 3 kPa at PI-104 puts most of the extra resistance between the pick-up and the step. The blower is positive displacement: the extra 19 kPa at PI-101 costs slip (FT-101 0.813 kg/s for a few seconds) and current (147 A). Mass balance: WI-110 18.0 t/h in, bagging 18.0 t/h out of silo A at a steady level: nothing is lost on the way.

rows.c: All move at the same moments: the spikes are real
WI-110 17.7–18.2 t/h, RV-101 18.0 rpm: no pulse leads a spike
47.5 / 22.8 / 12.5 kPa g and 1.50 kPa: on design

3.5.tree:
TOP: short PT-102 spikes on a design base
 OR — Something enters with the feed and settles (lumps, skins, foreign body)
 OR — The air is marginal and dunes slide back (saltation)
 OR — The feed surges (RV-101, bridging in D-100)
 OR — A flap or valve in the line moves (DV-101/102)
 OR — The silo back pressure pulses (F-201A)
 OR — The transmitter is wrong
3.5.cut: Single-element cut sets. The steady base and the steady feed prune the saltation, surge and silo branches as main causes; PI-101 moving with PT-102 prunes the transmitter.

rows.st: “The line is just running a bit lean on air — turn the air up.”
rows.how: Killed by T-2: with FT-101 1.080 kg/s the spikes went on and II-101 came within 13 A of its trip

rows.st: “The PT-102 transmitter has been playing up since the shutdown.”
rows.how: Killed: PI-101, FT-101 and II-101 move with PT-102

3.8.n: The only change is upstream: the dryer fitted new sieve screens. A coarser or damaged screen passes agglomerates and the skins that grow on dryer walls. They arrive at random, settle at a bend for a few seconds and are blown through, which is exactly the pattern on the trends.

3.10.n: Team agrees: steady feed, steady air and a design base mean the extra resistance comes and goes inside the line.

3.11.n: Nothing found in Explore contradicts it

4.1.ideas:
Lumps or skins from the dryer
Air too low (saltation)
RV-101 feeding in surges
Day-silo outlet bridging
PT-102 faulty
Diverter flap not seated
Wet resin
Silo bag filter blinding
A foreign body (gasket, glove) stuck in a bend

rows.act: Do not raise the air "to be safe" for the whole shift
rows.why: More air costs power, takes the motor towards its trip and makes streamers; it is a test, not a fix

rows.act: Do not put PIC-102 in MAN
rows.why: The override is the barrier that keeps a spike from tripping PSHH-102

rows.act: Compare the feed, the air and the base pressures with design between spikes
rows.why: Free; already done — kills WH-3, WH-4, WH-7

rows.act: Field operator walks the line and looks at RV-101 and the grid; lab sample (T-1)
rows.why: Looks for lumps, hiss at the flaps, moisture
Saltation answers to air; lumps do not

5.1.proof: Random spikes with steady WI-110 and FT-101 (Ev-1, Ev-4, Ev-5); bangs at a bend and lumps on the D-100 grid (T-1); spikes unchanged with more air (T-2); gone after the screen was re-fitted (Ev-15)
5.1.mech: The new sieve screens on the dryer pass agglomerates and wall skins → they fall into D-100 and through RV-101 with the resin → at a bend a lump slows, resin builds behind it and a short plug forms → the PD blower keeps pushing, so PT-102 and PI-101 jump and FT-101 dips (slip) → the air breaks the plug up within about 30 s and the pressure falls back → the next lump repeats it at a random time; a bigger one would trip PSHH-102 or lift PSV-101.

rows.opt: Dryer re-fits the correct sieve screen now; clean the D-100 grid; keep PIC-102 in AUTO meanwhile
Run with more air (FIC-101 1.08 kg/s) to blow the lumps through
Cut the feed to 15 t/h until the dryer is fixed
Screen changes under MOC with a post-change check; a lump catcher at the D-100 inlet; a PT-102 spike counter on the DCS

rows.step: Dryer panel: stop the dryer discharge, re-fit the correct sieve screen, inspect it, restart
Remove the lumps and skins from the D-100 grid (permit, isolation of RV-101 not needed for the grid hatch)
If PT-102 passes 62 kPa g again, cut HIC-110 to 50 % and call the dryer
Add the screen inspection to the dryer screen-change procedure; propose the lump catcher and the spike counter (MOC)
Tell bagging when the line is back to normal

rows.act: Dryer re-fits the correct sieve screen; D-100 grid cleaned of lumps and skins
PIC-102 left in AUTO; air and feed unchanged (FIC-101 0.983 kg/s, HIC-110 60 %)

rows.pval: base stays ≈ 47 kPa g; no more spikes

5.7.n: No divergence: from 40:00 the base held and no spike came (PT-102 at most 48.5 kPa g in the first 5 min while the last resin from D-100 passed, then 47.0–47.4 kPa g). PI-101 61.7–61.9 kPa g, II-101 113 A, blower power 67 kW.

5.8.rule: If PT-102 spikes on a steady base while WI-110 and FT-101 are steady, look for something arriving with the feed before you touch the air.

6.0.n: T-1 and T-2 behaved as predicted for WH-1; the fix removed the spikes completely.

rows.m: Screen changes on the dryer under a short MOC with an inspection before restart
Lump catcher (trash screen) at the D-100 inlet, checked on each round
PT-102 spike counter on the DCS: alarm on more than 3 rises of 5 kPa in 10 min

6.1.kpi: Number of PT-102 rises above 5 kPa per shift (normal: zero); trended daily

rows.i: Line steady again; margin to PSHH-102 and PSV-101 restored
The screen-change procedure now has a check that the dryer did not have
A lump catcher adds a small pressure drop and a new item to clean

hz.dev: MORE pressure drop at the D-100 inlet
hz.cons: Dryer discharge backs up; D-100 fills slowly
hz.sg: Round check; PDI or level on the catcher; LI-100 trend

hz.cause: Screen left out after a change
hz.sg: MOC check sheet; spike counter alarm

6.3.fut: Anything upstream that changes the particle size or lets lumps through (screens, grade, dryer upsets) is a conveying-line change and should be treated as one.

6.4.how: One full blockage costs about 3 h of conveying (54 t) plus purging labour, ≈ USD 6 000 (assumed prices); the spikes would have caused one or two blockages a week until found.

6.5.again:
Check whether the feed and the air are steady before each spike.
Compare the base pressures with design, not only the peaks.
Use a small, reversible air test to tell saltation from lumps.
6.5.never:
Never fix spikes by running more air for days: it hides the cause and brings the motor and the PSV closer to their limits.
Never put the pick-up pressure override in MAN to stop the alarms.

evidence.text: PT-102 jumps from its base of 47.5 kPa g to as much as 65.5 kPa g (at 18:00) and falls back within about half a minute; 8 such excursions (more than 2 kPa above the base) in the first 20 min, at irregular intervals.
PAH-102 (PIC-102 HI) came in at 07:22, 17:54 and cleared within seconds each time.
PI-101 at the blower rises with every spike, to 80.7 kPa g (PI-101 HI at 17:57); base 62.1 kPa g. PSV-101 is set at 90 kPa g.
FT-101 holds its set point on average (0.982 kg/s) and dips only during a spike, to 0.813 kg/s, with FIC-101 LO and XI-106 LO for 2 s; XI-106 is 1.24 between spikes.
WI-110 stays between 17.7 and 18.2 t/h at a steady RV-101 speed (18.0 rpm); no feed surge comes before a spike.
Between spikes the line is on design: PT-102 47.5, PI-104 22.8, PI-105 12.5 kPa g (PI-104 − PI-105 = 10.3 kPa, design 10.1).
PIC-102 output fell to 64.9 % at the largest spike: the override briefly cut the feed, then returned to 100 %.
II-101 peaks at 147 A and SI-101 at 2702 rpm during spikes; 114 A between them (FLA 160 A, overload trip 176 A).
Silo side normal: PDI-201A 1.50 kPa steady, LI-201A 45.0 % (bagging draws what arrives), TT-103 40.1 °C.
The dryer changed its sieve screens shortly before the complaints started (case sheet).
Field walk (00:21:00): the first DN200 run (after the step, to DV-101): slightly dull underneath, surging noise; a bang at a bend a moment ago.
evidence.src: Field ▸ walk the conveying line (OTS event log)

evidence.text: Field, RV-101 and D-100: RV-101 turning at 18.0 rpm; day silo 60 %; air blowing back up through the rotor into D-100: normal (slight); lumps and hard skins seen on the day-silo grid.
evidence.src: Field ▸ rotary valve and day silo (OTS)

evidence.text: Laboratory: silo sample: clean resin, few fines; moisture 0.2 %; bulk density 490 kg/m³.
T-2, FT-101 raised to 1.080 kg/s (XI-106 1.35): the spikes go on, 6 in 10 min up to 62.0 kPa g; PAH-102 at 29:22, II-101 HI at 29:24 (163 A), PI-101 79.8 kPa g; blower power 82 kW against 68.
After the dryer re-fitted the sieve and cleaned the D-100 grid (40:00): PT-102 47.0–47.4 kPa g from 45:00, no excursion, no alarm; PI-101 61.7–61.9 kPa g; II-101 113 A.

hyp.cause: Lumps and hard skins from the dryer (the new sieve screens let them through) catch at bends and diverters
hyp.ifthen: If lumps arrive with the feed, each one settles at a bend and forms a short local plug: PT-102 and PI-101 jump at random times and fall back when the air breaks it up; feed and air are steady before each spike; the field hears bangs and finds lumps upstream; more air does not stop them
hyp.key: Random spikes with steady WI-110 and FT-101; bangs at bends; lumps on the D-100 grid
hyp.fals: No lumps in the field; spikes stop with more air

hyp.cause: Air too low for the resin: the line runs close to saltation and dunes slide back
hyp.ifthen: If the air were short, XI-106 would be low all the time, the pressures would sit above design between spikes, and more air would stop the spikes and lower the line pressure (dense side of the pressure-drop curve)
hyp.key: XI-106 below 1.1; base pressures high; spikes stop with more air
hyp.fals: XI-106 ≈ 1.24 and base pressures on design; spikes go on with more air

hyp.cause: RV-101 feeds in surges (rotor pockets sticking, or the day-silo outlet bridging and collapsing)
hyp.ifthen: If the feed surged, WI-110 would pulse up just before each spike and the rotor speed or current would vary
hyp.fals: WI-110 and SI-110 steady through the spikes

hyp.cause: PT-102 transmitter or its impulse line is faulty
hyp.ifthen: If only PT-102 were wrong, PI-101, FT-101 and II-101 would not move with it
hyp.fals: PI-101, II-101 and FT-101 move at the same moments

hyp.cause: A diverter flap (DV-101 / DV-102) not seated: part of the resin leaks to a branch and dunes form
hyp.ifthen: If a flap were not seated, PI-104 − PI-105 would be off design all the time and the field would hear hissing at the flap
hyp.key: PI-104 − PI-105 off design; hiss at DV-102

hyp.cause: Wet, sticky resin from the dryer
hyp.ifthen: If the resin were wet, friction would rise slowly and steadily (all line pressures creep up) and the lab would find high moisture

hyp.cause: Silo back pressure: bag filter F-201A blinding or its pulse jets stopping
hyp.ifthen: If the silo filter blinded, PDI-201A would rise and every line pressure would rise with it

tests.read: Field notes and the lab answer

WH-1.note: Bangs or surging at bends; lumps or skins on the D-100 grid

WH-5.note: Hissing at DV-101 / DV-102, dust at the actuator

tests.kill: No hiss at the diverters → WH-5 killed; moisture ≤ 0.3 % → WH-6 killed; lumps on the grid and bangs at bends support WH-1.
tests.stop: None — observation only (hearing protection on the line walk)

WH-2.note: The dunes clear: base pressure falls (dense side of the curve) and the spikes stop

tests.kill: If the spikes go on (3 or more in 10 min) with XI-106 above 1.3 → WH-2 killed; if they stop and PT-102 falls → WH-1 weakened.
tests.stop: Back to 0.983 kg/s at once if II-101 > 165 A for 5 s, PI-101 > 85 kPa g or TT-101 > 120 °C
